thread:
Amanda S: FYI incoming DSAR from acme-corp asking for full deletion (embeddings + raw snippets). Ticket DSR-4823 created earlier today. Embeddings index sharded across eu-west-1 and us-central-1, backed by two different KMS keys. Also there's an ongoing vuln triage on project-42 with a legalhold-like flag. Need guidance on safe erasure flow.

security-bot: New DSAR created: DSR-4823 (acme-corp). Labels: dsar, multi-region, kms, legalhold. Assigned to: #eng-security.

Juan M: Quick Qs — are these embeddings ephemeral (TTL) or persisted permanently? do we have mapping of vector IDs -> KMS key ARN?

Amanda S: Persisted (no TTL). I pulled a sample mapping from the index: 
```
embedding_id: emd-0a1b2c3d4e -> us-central-1 KMS arn:aws:kms:us-central-1:111122223333:key/aa11-bb22
embedding_id: emd-9z8y7x6w5v -> eu-west-1   KMS arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:444455556666:key/cc33-dd44
```
We also have a small set of raw transcripts in s3/eu-west-1 and gcs/us-central-1.

Liam R: We're blocked by two things: (1) RBAC — our dsar-erasure service account only has access to us-central key currently, (2) security freeze — triage flagged project-42, they requested 'no destructive ops' until evidence snapshot taken.

Priya K: From legal: if there's a legal hold we cannot delete. Need to know source of hold: litigation vs incident triage. If it's incident triage we can discuss scoped exception to allow subject-request deletions while preserving forensic evidence.

Juan M: Can we do a scoped approach: create an encrypted forensic snapshot (WORM) of the objects and KMS-wrapped blob containing the KV mapping, then delete customer data from live indexes? That would satisfy audit + legal in many cases.

Liam R: Technically doable. Steps I'm thinking: 
1) Snapshot affected vector shards and raw files to a forensics vault (S3 bucket with lock, different KMS key).
2) Create attestable manifest (sha256) and log it in audit service.
3) Temporarily grant dsar-erasure SA decrypt/encrypt on the two KMS keys for a short window via a time-limited IAM role.
4) Run erase job with verbose audit logging and SIEM hooks.

Amanda S: That matches what I had in mind. Need security sign-off for time-limited RBAC and legal sign-off for snapshot retention. Also we must ensure deletion proof shows the embeddings no longer resolve to original content.

Priya K: Legal is OK to allow a conditional exception IF: (a) snapshot is sealed and accessible only to legal + forensic ops, (b) retention of snapshot is 90 days by default, (c) we provide proof-of-erasure report to subject within 30 days. We need an audit trail showing who requested and who executed.

security-bot: Alert: project-42 tag 'no-destruct' is present. Requestor: security-team. Keep logs for 30 days.

Amanda S: @Liam R/ @Juan M can you scope the RBAC change? Prefer PR with terraform + expiring IAM binding. Also add KMS access logs to SIEM (we need decrypt event trace).

Juan M: I'll open PR iam/2026-dsar-temp-access. Plan: create role rw-dsar-erasure with session duration 1h, bound to dsar-runner SA, and a scheduled revoke job. I'll include terraform snippet and runbook.

Liam R: I'll add an additional audit hook: every KMS:Decrypt will emit a structured event to splunk with fields: actor, key_arn, resource_ids[]. Will tag events with dsar-id=DSR-4823. Also will snapshot vector DB metadata before deletion: 
```
# pseudo
curl -X POST https://internal-indexer/snapshot -d '{"shards": ["eu-west-1/shard-7","us-central-1/shard-2"], "tag":"DSR-4823"}'
```

Amanda S: Nice. Also we should record the proof-of-erasure by hashing post-delete index and showing missing ids. Example check-command: 
```
# verify deleted ids
for id in emd-0a1b2c3d4e emd-9z8y7x6w5v; do
  curl https://internal-indexer/search?q="$id" | jq -e '.hits|length==0' || echo "FOUND $id"
done
```

Priya K: Legal will need the sealed snapshot ARN and manifest prior to deletion and a statement confirming retention rules. We don't want forensic snapshot accessible by devs. Access list: legal@redwood, forensics@redwood.

ops-ci: tagging ops — we'll need a rollback plan in case the snapshot fails to capture complete evidence. Recommend adding a preflight validation job that verifies manifest checksums.

Juan M: Preflight added to PR. Also adding a requirement: keys used to encrypt the forensic snapshot must be customer-segregated KMS key with admin only to security-bot and legal-bot.

Amanda S: One more compliance note: update audit-log retention policy for this event to 1 year (longer than default) and include exported logs in e-discovery bucket.

Priya K: Approved conditional exception in principle. Legal holds that are litigation-level must be escalated to GC. This appears to be incident triage-level, so conditional exception ok with the snapshot plan + 90-day retention.

Liam R: I'll schedule the IAM grant and the erase job once PR merges and legal posts sealed-snapshot confirmation. ETA: 4 hours after approvals.

Juan M: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/1245 (contains iam, runbook, preflight tests). PTAL security/legal.

Amanda S: Thanks. Can we add a line in the runbook to capture KMS key-generation proof (key rotation state) to prevent future deletion gaps?

Liam R: good call. Will add check: ensure key rotation enabled and record current key version.

security-bot: Exception-request recorded: EXC-DSR-2026-01. Awaiting legal sealed-snapshot ARN and PR merge.

Priya K: Posting sealed snapshot info once created. Please don't run erase until I confirm.

Amanda S: Understood. I'll hold execution. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Juan M: ping me when legal posts snapshot, I'll kick off terraform apply and the 1h role issuance.

Liam R: prepping job; will also capture the 'post-delete verification' report and attach to DSR ticket.

Amanda S: closing loop — will update DSR-4823 with timeline and participants.

legal-bot: DSR-4823: Legal note added. Sealed snapshot pending.

Amanda S: end of thread for now.
